screen.neurolab.guide.subtitle: Controls, movement, learning, and what the signals mean
screen.neurolab.guide.scroll: Scroll to read · Esc to close
screen.neurolab.guide.q1: How do I start a Neuro Fly?
screen.neurolab.guide.a1: Use its Creative spawn egg or run /summon neurolab:neuro_fly. It attaches after the connectome finishes loading.
screen.neurolab.guide.q2: Can I attach a brain to another mob?
screen.neurolab.guide.a2: Yes. Run /neurolab attach <entity selector>; for example, /neurolab attach @e[type=minecraft:sheep,limit=1,sort=nearest]. Assisted mode keeps ordinary mob AI active and adds bounded steering; Neuro Fly uses its dedicated flight controller. Neural mode takes full control, and observe mode records without moving the mob.
screen.neurolab.guide.q3: Can every mob fly, and how high can Neuro Fly go?
screen.neurolab.guide.a3: Only mobs that already have a flying body receive vertical commands. Neuro Fly tracks a modest height above terrain in assisted mode. Existing mobs keep their own movement or flying speed cap.
screen.neurolab.guide.q4: What do pain and reward mean in Minecraft?
screen.neurolab.guide.a4: Damage, fire, rain, harmful blocks and close threats can signal pain; plants, water, exploration and health recovery can signal reward. Green + and red - above an attached mob show the current signals. These are game-world proxies, not biological measurements.
screen.neurolab.guide.q5: Does the brain learn from those signals?
screen.neurolab.guide.a5: Reward and pain adjust recently active directed connectome edges within strict limits. A small sparse state is saved with the mob. This experimental rule is not a validated biological learning model.
screen.neurolab.guide.q6: How do I see through a mob?
screen.neurolab.guide.a6: The top-right HUD follows a nearby tracked brain. Aim at a brain-attached mob and press V to pin its first-person view; press V again to return. The Neuro Viewer item works too. Press I to toggle the HUD.
screen.neurolab.guide.q7: Where are the analysis and panel settings?
screen.neurolab.guide.a7: Press Ctrl+N for the analysis popup, then SETTINGS to choose side panels and plots. Press H for this guide. Key bindings can be changed in Minecraft Controls.
screen.neurolab.guide.q8: The dashboard is empty or the mob does not move. What now?
screen.neurolab.guide.a8: Wait for connectome loading, then check /neurolab status. Use /neurolab inspect on the mob and confirm client and server run the same mod version. Observe mode intentionally does not move the mob.
screen.neurolab.guide.q9: How do I attach a brain to another mob?
screen.neurolab.guide.a9: Hold the Neural Brain Attacher and right-click the target mob directly. If the connectome is still loading, try again in a moment.
screen.neurolab.guide.q10: What does the Neuro Monitor block show?
screen.neurolab.guide.a10: Right-click the Neuro Monitor to open its live lab console. Link a mob within 6 blocks, choose one of six electrodes, deliver a bounded pulse, change control mode, and view eye/touch/motor traces plus spike and synapse counts. The console runs without pausing the world.
screen.neurolab.guide.q11: Where can I tune light and fly behavior?
screen.neurolab.guide.a11: Open NeuroLab configuration from the Mods menu. Server-side settings include balanced/light/shade response, cruise throttle, flower-search radius, animal/villager perching, and rain shelter seeking.
screen.neurolab.guide.q12: How do I use the experiment chair?
screen.neurolab.guide.a12: Place the Neuro Experiment Chair near a mob and right-click to attach and dock the subject. The chair is only a subject fixture; use the Neuro Monitor or stimulus probes for measurements and test input. Sneak-right-click clears it.
